subject: Expansion econ: bridge plan + new route qualification
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@paymesh.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus@paymesh.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expansion follow-up — token economics and new route

Kim — thanks for the productive call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move to PO: 

- Volume profile: seasonally ramping from ~600K tokens/day to ~2.2M tokens/day over 6 months (peaks expected in Nov).
- Primary workload: customer chat + short-form summaries (~12–50 tokens per call) + a smaller embeddings path for search (embed-lite).
- What we need from Redwood: target blended $/1M tokens for the proposed mix below, any short-term bridge/credits to smooth Q3 spend, and confirmation that adding a separate "fast-text" route (lower-latency lower-precision model) is supported under the same contract.

Target commercial constraints from Paymesh finance: internal target is $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens for the blended mix. We understand exact number depends on routing and caching. Please confirm if the range is feasible and outline assumptions (batching, cache hit %, model types).

I've attached our initial forecast and a rough traffic split — happy to jump on a short call next week to finalize the mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform — Paymesh
(elena@paymesh.com)

Attachment: paymesh_forecast_q3q4.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@paymesh.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus@paymesh.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expansion follow-up — token economics and new route

Elena — thanks for the note and the file. Good align from the call. Below is a concise econ summary and next steps so we have a single place to iterate: 

1) Assumptions that went into these ranges:
   - Model mix: 70% text-gen (raven-medium), 20% fast-text (raven-fast, lower precision), 10% embeddings (embed-lite).
   - Avg token per gen call: 28 tokens.
   - Cache hit estimate: 12% prefix hits (savings applied to gen path).
   - Typical batching (hosted): effective throughput improvements x1.6 at peak.

2) Proposed commercial options (blended):
   - Option A (aggressive): $880 per 1M tokens — requires 12-month commit at current ramp profile + route-add (fast-text) enabled; includes one-time Q3 bridge credit equal to 5% of month 1 invoice.
   - Option B (conservative): $1,050 per 1M tokens — monthly rolling with a 3-month minimum term; no bridge credit, higher per-token price but flexible scale.

3) Dedicated capacity note: if you expect sustained >1.8M tokens/day we should consider a dedicated pool (saves ~18% on per-token at scale due to reserved capacity efficiencies).

4) Next steps I propose:
   - We circulate the attached pricing model (paymesh_pricing_v2.xlsx) for your finance team to validate.
   - If Option A is acceptable, Marissa will prepare a draft SOW + pricing appendix and I will draft the DocuSign for signatures.
   - If Paymesh prefers Option B, we can go live sooner with a short canary for the fast-text route.

I've attached our consolidated model (paymesh_pricing_v2.xlsx) and a two-page one-pager that explains how the bridge credit is applied. Happy to hop on a 30-min call Tue/Wed to finalize.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: paymesh_pricing_v2.xlsx, proposed_mop_consolidated.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Expansion follow-up — token economics and new route

Kim / Marissa — quick internal:

- Option A looks doable from a capacity planning POV. We can allocate a small reserved slice for the first 60 days of the ramp to ensure the fast-text route gets stable latency SLAs during canary. That keeps the cost math in the $860–$900 effective range after credits if they hit the ramp.
- We should add an SLA caveat for the fast-text route: 99th p50 latencies measured per-route; if we see >15% variance we fall back to raven-medium. Operations will own the fallback.
- For renewals: recommend building a 9–12 month check-in metric (token volume and cache effectiveness) to reset blended bands — keeps the blended rate fair as their traffic profile matures.

Marissa — can you draft the SOW appendix for Option A and include the fallback mechanics + canary acceptance criteria? I'll sign off once it's drafted.

Thanks,
Dylan
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
